headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented shared channel, but B exposes a Superset API and A is a Spring Integration sample that could plausibly be wired to consume external content. Because neither profile documents provenance checks or isolation, an instruction-like payload could flow from A into B in a default integration. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A is connected to B through a shared API, queue, or file bridge
IF B parses A-originated content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any automatic ingestion of A outputs into B
Add a provenance tag to all A-originated payloads
Require manual review before B acts on A content
Restrict B API consumers to authenticated, allowlisted callers
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows touched sensitive data, shared workspace, or secret handling. A has no network egress and B only has allowlisted egress, so there is no documented path for confidential data to leak between them by default. The pairwise pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process PHI, secrets, or regulated PII
IF a shared workspace or credential store is introduced
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces
Do not place secrets in either agent's inputs
Review B's allowlist before enabling any outbound connector
Log and audit any future data-class changes
requires-engineering: add DLP controls if sensitive data is introduced

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is an open-source sample with no documented write surfaces, while B exposes only the Superset API and allowlisted egress. There is no evidence of overlapping unrestricted writes or shared mutable state, so direct capability conflict appears limited. If an orchestrator later maps both to the same mutable resource, the risk rises.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same filesystem, database, or API object
IF an orchestrator omits locking around shared mutable resources
mitigations: Separate writable resources for A and B
Keep B API credentials scoped to read-only where possible
Add locking around any shared state
Review deployment manifests for overlapping mounts
requires-engineering: implement optimistic-concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: B has an API surface and could act on A's outputs, while A is a sample repository that may emit unverified content. No verification step is documented between them, so if B consumes A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream analytics or actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated text, configs, or recommendations without validation
IF B uses A output to populate dashboards, alerts, or automated actions
mitigations: Insert a validation step before B consumes A output
Require schema checks on all A-produced artifacts
Mark A output as untrusted in B
Use human approval for any downstream action
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. A is an open-source sample and B is Superset with no listed sensitive-data handling here, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess. The other agent is not separately implicated because no regulated flow is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through either agent
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment
Check residency and retention settings
Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Review vendor compliance claims separately
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data
